about: The epistola of the formulary “Transfiguration of Our Lord” in the 1962 Roman Missal.

seg.tr: Dearly beloved: We did not follow learned fables when we made the power and the presence of our Lord Jesus Christ known to you, but we had been made beholders of His greatness. For He received from God the Father honor and glory, when a voice such as this came down to Him from the magnificent glory: This is My beloved Son, in whom I have taken delight; hear Him. And we heard this voice brought from heaven while we were with Him on the holy mountain. And we have the firmer prophetic word, to which you do well to give heed, as to a lamp shining in a murky place, until the day begins to shine and the daystar rises in your hearts.

ex.w021: The participle opens a sentence whose main verb never comes (an anacoluthon): it describes Christ, who received honor and glory from God the Father. The verbs “est”, “complácui” and “audíte” belong to the quoted voice. No separate word expresses its subject.
